title: Nominal day on station

mission.where: Low Earth orbit, inside the magnetosphere

description: Routine operations with a short payload task. Use it to learn the normal ranges.

title: Nominal day at the lunar base

mission.where: Lunar south-pole surface habitat, no magnetosphere

description: Routine work in 0.17 g. Heart rate and blood pressure sit a little higher than on the ISS because gravity pulls blood towards the legs again; background radiation is higher without a magnetosphere.

title: Nominal sol at the Mars base

mission.where: Mars surface habitat; thin CO2 atmosphere shields part of the radiation

description: Routine work in 0.38 g. The cardiovascular system carries more load than in orbit; ground support is 12 minutes away.

title: Fatigue → microsleep

mission.where: Low Earth orbit, inside the magnetosphere

description: Night-shift robotic-arm monitoring. EEG slowing rises minutes before head nods and microsleeps.

title: Fatigue → microsleep

mission.where: Lunar south-pole surface habitat, no magnetosphere

description: Lunar night: 14 days of darkness blur the sleep–wake rhythm. EEG slowing rises minutes before head nods and microsleeps.

title: Fatigue → microsleep (sol shift)

mission.where: Mars surface habitat; thin CO2 atmosphere shields part of the radiation

description: The 24 h 39 min Martian sol keeps shifting the schedule; drowsiness starts earlier than on the ISS.

title: Cognitive overload

mission.where: Low Earth orbit, inside the magnetosphere

description: Docking of a visiting vehicle with multiple malfunctions: workload index, HR, BP and skin conductance rise; HRV falls.

title: Cognitive overload (manual landing)

mission.where: Human landing system, final descent to the lunar surface

description: Final descent with a failed landing sensor: the commander flies the last 500 m by hand among boulders.

title: Cognitive overload (medical emergency, no ground help)

mission.where: Mars surface habitat; thin CO2 atmosphere shields part of the radiation

description: A crewmate is injured; with a 24-min round trip the crew handles the emergency alone.

title: Hypoxia (slow cabin leak)

mission.where: Low Earth orbit, inside the magnetosphere

description: Undetected depressurisation: ppO2, SpO2 and brain oxygenation fall; crew dons O2 mask at 11:30.

title: Hypoxia (slow habitat leak)

mission.where: Lunar south-pole surface habitat, no magnetosphere

description: Abrasive lunar dust wears a hatch seal: slow leak, ppO2, SpO2 and brain oxygenation fall; crew dons O2 mask at 11:30.

title: Hypoxia (slow habitat leak)

mission.where: Mars surface habitat; thin CO2 atmosphere shields part of the radiation

description: A cracked seal in the cold Martian night leaks air; ppO2, SpO2 and brain oxygenation fall; crew dons O2 mask at 11:30.

title: High-G / G-LOC precursor

mission.where: Capsule re-entry to Earth after a long stay in microgravity

description: Return to Earth after 6 months on the ISS, with an abort-profile load peak: brain oxygenation (fNIRS) falls with sustained +Gz.

title: High-G / G-LOC precursor

mission.where: Orion skip entry to Earth on the way back from the Moon

description: Orion returns from the Moon at 11 km/s; the skip entry peaks higher than an ISS return.

title: High-G / G-LOC precursor (deconditioned crew)

mission.where: Mars entry, descent & landing after 7 months in microgravity

description: Mars entry after 7 months in microgravity: the peak G is lower than an Earth entry, but deconditioning lowers G tolerance, so brain oxygen still falls fast.

title: Spatial disorientation

mission.where: Low Earth orbit, inside the magnetosphere

description: Visual reorientation illusion when moving between modules with different 'up' directions; weaker than on a planetary surface.

title: Spatial disorientation

mission.where: Pressurised rover traverse on the Moon

description: Rover traverse in 0.17 g: weak gravity cues and long shadows make tilt and slope hard to judge.

title: Spatial disorientation

mission.where: Pressurised rover traverse on Mars

description: Rover traverse soon after landing: the inner ear is still adapting from 7 months of microgravity to 0.38 g.

title: CO2 build-up (scrubber failure)

mission.where: Low Earth orbit, inside the magnetosphere

description: CO2 removal (CDRA) fails; respiration, HR and BP rise, drowsiness/headache markers follow.

title: CO2 build-up (scrubber failure)

mission.where: Lunar south-pole surface habitat, no magnetosphere

description: Lunar dust clogs the CO2 scrubber; respiration, HR and BP rise, drowsiness/headache markers follow.

title: CO2 build-up (scrubber failure)

mission.where: Mars surface habitat; thin CO2 atmosphere shields part of the radiation

description: CO2 scrubber fails with no resupply possible; respiration, HR and BP rise, drowsiness/headache markers follow.

title: Hypoglycaemia after exercise

mission.where: Low Earth orbit, inside the magnetosphere

description: Exercise after a skipped meal; glucose falls below 70 then 54 mg/dL, recovers after 15 g carbs.

title: Hypoglycaemia after exercise

mission.where: Lunar south-pole surface habitat, no magnetosphere

description: Heavy shovelling of regolith after a skipped meal; glucose falls below 70 then 54 mg/dL, recovers after 15 g carbs.

title: Hypoglycaemia after exercise

mission.where: Mars surface habitat; thin CO2 atmosphere shields part of the radiation

description: Treadmill session in 0.38 g after a skipped meal; glucose falls below 70 then 54 mg/dL, recovers after 15 g carbs.

title: Fever / immune response

mission.where: Low Earth orbit, inside the magnetosphere

description: Latent virus reactivation (time-compressed): temperature, HR and respiration rise, HRV falls.

title: Fever / immune response

mission.where: Lunar south-pole surface habitat, no magnetosphere

description: Latent virus reactivation (time-compressed); evacuation to Earth would take about 3 days.

title: Fever / immune response

mission.where: Mars surface habitat; thin CO2 atmosphere shields part of the radiation

description: Latent virus reactivation (time-compressed); no evacuation possible, the Crew Medical Officer treats on site.

title: Solar particle event (magnetosphere shields)

mission.where: Low Earth orbit, inside the magnetosphere

description: The same solar storm seen from the ISS: Earth's magnetic field deflects most protons, so the dose rate rises only to the caution band.

title: Solar particle event

mission.where: Lunar south-pole surface habitat, no magnetosphere

description: No magnetosphere: the full proton storm reaches the surface; crew moves to the storm shelter and dose rate drops.

title: Solar particle event (thin atmosphere)

mission.where: Mars surface habitat; thin CO2 atmosphere shields part of the radiation

description: Mars' thin atmosphere absorbs part of the storm; dose still exceeds the alert limit, crew shelters.

title: EVA: decompression sickness risk

mission.where: Spacewalk outside the ISS

description: Spacewalk after a shortened O2 prebreathe: tissue N2 ratio is high at 29.6 kPa suit pressure; a suit pressure bump resolves it.

title: Moonwalk: decompression sickness risk

mission.where: Moonwalk from the lunar base

description: Habitat at 70.3 kPa (26.5 % O2) shortens prebreathe, but walking in 0.17 g works the joints harder than floating, and the prebreathe was skipped.

title: Mars EVA: decompression sickness risk

mission.where: Surface EVA from the Mars base

description: Habitat at 70.3 kPa; walking in 0.38 g is heavy work in the suit and the prebreathe was skipped.

title: Cabin heat & humidity (thermal-control failure)

mission.where: Low Earth orbit, inside the magnetosphere

description: Coolant pump fails: cabin temperature, humidity and fan noise rise; heart rate and body temperature follow.

title: Cabin heat (lunar day, radiator failure)

mission.where: Lunar south-pole surface habitat, no magnetosphere

description: At lunar noon the surface reaches +120 °C; a radiator pump fails and the cabin heats faster than on the ISS.

title: Cold cabin (heater failure at night)

mission.where: Mars surface habitat; thin CO2 atmosphere shields part of the radiation

description: Night at −80 °C outside: the heater bus fails and the cabin cools; shivering raises heart rate and blood pressure.
